Maya: Heads-up: customer reported an overcharge when a streaming session reconnected during an in-flight toolcall (doc_search). They saw stream tokens + tool tokens billed.
Sam: Hmm. Which piece emitted the tool tokens? Runtime or tool proxy?
Jordan: Runtime sends a toolcall event and the ledger writes tokens on event emission. On reconnect the runtime re-emitted the same logical step because we replay seq ranges; there was no stable tool identifier, so ledger treated it as a second tool invocation.
Lee: Right now dedupe keys are (session_id, seq). That fails when reconnect replay includes the same seq but lacks a tool-specific id. We need a persistent toolcall id.
Maya: Example snippet from trace: 
```
STREAM_EVENT {session: "u-77", seq_start: 120}
TOOL_CALL {name: "doc_search", args: {...}}  <-- no uuid
...disconnect...
STREAM_REPLAY {session: "u-77", seq_start: 120}
TOOL_CALL {name: "doc_search", args: {...}}  <-- replayed
```
Sam: Billing impact question: if we surface provisional tokens in Console, do they count against customer quota + hard limits? Finance wants clarity.
Jordan: Proposal: write a provisional ledger row for toolcalls keyed by toolcall_uuid and mark settled when tool returns (tool_final=true). Dedupe via unique index on toolcall_uuid. UI shows provisional tokens separate from settled.
Lee: Alternative: delay charging tool tokens until tool_final seen. But that changes observability (customers will see lower live usage until settle) and complicates rate-limiting decisions that rely on immediate charges.
Maya: Can we compromise: provisional holds reduce available quota (so hard limits respected) but are flagged and excluded from billing until settled? Then if they never settle within window, we convert to billed or expire.
Sam: That seems workable. Need rules: provisional timeout (T_expire) and conversion policy. Finance prefers short timeouts to avoid long ambiguous holds. Maybe T_expire = 20s for toolcalls, with a convert-to-bill at +2s to allow late commits.
Jordan: Telemetry: add counters: streaming_toolcall_emitted, toolcall_uuid_dedupe, provisional_to_settled, provisional_expired. Also histogram for provisional latency. We'll need these to tune T_expire.
Lee: Routing concern: if request is routed to fallback region/model and runtime replays the toolcall on fallback, it must carry the same toolcall_uuid. Make sure router attaches/forwards the uuid on cross-route handoffs.
Maya: Good point. Add a router invariant: preserve toolcall_uuid across reroutes and model substitutions. Document in RFC.
Sam: UX for console: request detail panel shows three rows: Stream tokens, Tool tokens (Settled), Tool tokens (Provisional). Use color tint and tooltip: "Provisional: awaiting tool completion. May be converted or refunded." Small lock icon when provisional reduces quota.
Lee: Implementation notes: 1) StreamEvent proto add optional string toolcall_uuid and bool toolcall_finalized; 2) Ledger write path checks toolcall_uuid and upserts provisional row; 3) Short TTL index on provisional rows; 4) Reconciliation job to sweep expired provisionals and apply convert/expire policy.
Jordan: Tests: cross-route dedupe e2e, provisional TTL fuzz test, charge-visibility integration test with Console snapshots. Add canary rollout to 10% to validate no regressions in billing spikes.
billing-bot: Created BILL-805 with tag "provisional-toolcall" for finance review.
Maya: I'll draft RFC with proto diff + console mock + migration plan. Target review by Thu. Attaching perf note: provisional path must not add >1ms p50 to runtime path.
Sam: Finance ok with provisional hold reducing quota as long as conversion window <= 30s and we show clear UX. We'll review BILL-805 once RFC lands.
Lee: I'll mock Console panel and edge-case tooltip copy.
Jordan: I'll add telemetry hooks and a feature flag to gate dedupe-on-uuid.
Maya: Action items: RFC (Maya), proto patch (Jordan), console mock (Lee), finance signoff (Sam). Follow-up sync Wed 09:30.
